Hi Alex / Sarah —

Thanks again for the time today — great discussion on how FinServCo plans to integrate Redwood for structured responses and embeddings-powered reranking. Per our call, wanted to recap the recommended auth approaches and next steps so your engineering team can evaluate: 

Summary of recommended options (short):
- Server-side service account + short-lived JWTs (recommended): service account credentials live in your KMS/HSM; exchange for short-lived bearer tokens via client credentials flow.
- Static API keys: OK for quick POCs but not for production (risk if embedded in client apps).
- OAuth2 (3-legged) for end-user delegation: useful if FinServCo needs user-scoped actions tied to their identity.

Key implementation notes we covered:
- SDK setup: call patterns are identical across hosted/dedicated/private; use server-side SDKs for generation/embedding/alternative rerank calls. Example header: Authorization: Bearer <short-lived-token> or x-api-key for legacy keys.
- Routing: use per-route model pinning for sensitive endpoints; add header x-redwood-key-role to indicate service account role for routing/quotas.
- Structured output & tool-calling: recommend enabling strict schema enforcement on the Redwood SDK to avoid hallucinated tool calls; sign tool invocation payloads with service account token.
- Embeddings/rerankers: do embedding generation and reranking server-side behind your proxy to avoid exposing keys.

Next steps (action items):
1) Dev: confirm whether FinServCo wants service accounts (recommended) or to try short-lived API keys for POC — due 6/12
2) Rishi: send technical notes + key-rotation playbook and stub code for token exchange — I cc'd him.
3) Alex: share the internal security questionnaire (if you want, attach) — we can map answers to our private deployment checklist.

Attachments: I attached the high-level key rotation playbook and your questionnaire stub from the call.

If useful, we can set a 30-min follow-up with Dev and Rishi to walk through the token exchange flow and sample SDK calls.

Best,
Marissa

Hi Alex — I'm Dev (Engineering, Redwood) — quick answers inline and a minimal recipe for a zero-downtime rotation. See attached 'redwood-key-rotation-playbook.md' for full steps.

1) TTL: 15 minutes is fine for high-sensitivity endpoints. For most server-to-server calls we recommend 15-60m depending on your threat model; refresh tokens are kept in your KMS.

2) Zero-downtime rotation (summary):
- Dual-key strategy: provision new key (K2) alongside current key (K1).
- Update proxy layer to accept both keys and tag requests with x-redwood-key-version.
- Gradually roll producers to K2. Once all traffic validated, retire K1 after a grace period.
- For multi-region: do staged rollouts region-by-region while keeping universal acceptance at the Redwood ingress for both versions.

Example headers we recommend:
- Authorization: Bearer <jwt> (preferred)
- x-redwood-key-version: v20280612
- x-redwood-key-role: embeddings-only

3) Scoped keys: yes — Redwood supports key-scopes/roles. You can issue an embeddings-only service account that has a scope limited to embeddings.create + embeddings.search/rerank. That key will fail on text-generation endpoints.

Minimal IAM surface (on your side):
- KMS: decrypt (for service account private key) and IAM: serviceAccountTokenCreator (if using GCP-style SA exchange).
- Proxy: read-only access to key metadata and ability to call the token exchange endpoint.

Attached: redwood-key-rotation-playbook.md (contains curl and SDK snippets), and a sample node/python exchange flow.

If it helps, we can run a 30-min hands-on with your SREs this week to demo a rotation and token exchange.

Regards,
